mode: actual X11 screen capture of a dedicated Kitty window; actual Neovim, Rust server, and Pi adapter
model: Pi faux provider with fixed responses; no provider credentials supplied
tools: no tools in this first-run demonstration; tool execution is covered by the actual terminal integration tests
input: keys sent to the terminal with Kitty remote control
capture: FFmpeg x11grab restricted to the terminal window

steps.text: Run ./harness.sh from your project. No configuration file or API key is present.
Press ; to open the tree. The empty state explains how to begin.
Press n. Setup opens before the agent name is requested.
Choose 2 for the local demo. It uses fixed replies and needs no API key.
Enter review as the agent name. The prompt opens ready for typing.
Type a task. Ctrl-S sends it; Enter adds a line while you type.
Read the reply. The demo label states that no AI model is connected.
Move back to your source file with normal Neovim window commands.
Press ; twice to focus the tree. Press g whenever you want to change setup.
Press Enter on review to return to its saved conversation and prompt.
Press Escape, then :qa to close. Settings and conversation remain saved.
For AI coding, choose Anthropic in setup, select a model, and enter your API key.

assertions: normal editor starts with one window
semicolon shows an empty project tree and next steps
n opens setup before asking for an agent name
explicit demo choice saves configuration without credentials
named agent is selected and input mode begins
multiline task appears in the stored transcript
fixed demo answer appears and reaches idle
saved agent can be selected from the tree
cleanup: all demonstration sessions stopped; private server shut down; terminal closed
